source.title: Recent results and open problems on parabolic equations with gradient nonlinearities

accepted.question_text: Consider the semilinear parabolic initial-boundary value problem u_t - Δu = |u|^{p-1}u - b|∇u|^q on a domain Ω ⊂ R^N with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions, where p > 1, q ≥ 1, and b > 0. In the whole space Ω = R^N, focus on the scaling-critical case q = 2p/(p+1) with b small. For the pure reaction-diffusion equation u_t - Δu = |u|^{p-1}u, the Fujita exponent p_c = 1 + 2/N separates the regime where every nontrivial nonnegative solution blows up from the regime where positive global solutions exist. Does an analogous Fujita critical exponent exist for this gradient-damped equation in R^N when q = 2p/(p+1) and b is small?
accepted.context_brief: Fujita critical exponent for the gradient-damped model in R^N

evidence.quote: Open problem 1. Is there a Fujita critical exponent for equation (1.6) in R^N when q = 2p/(p + 1) and b is small?

For equation (1.1) in Ω = R^N a classical result, essentially due to Fujita (see [20, 33]), asserts that no nonnegative nontrivial global solutions exist for p ≤ 1 + 2/N, whereas both blowing-up and global positive solutions do exist if p > 1 + 2/N. The value pc = 1 + 2/N is thus said to be the Fujita critical exponent of the problem.

accepted.question_text: Let Ω be a domain containing a cone Ω_0, and consider the same parabolic problem u_t - Δu = |u|^{p-1}u - b|∇u|^q with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions. Theorem 2.5 proves finite-time blowup under the lower-growth-at-infinity condition lim inf_{|x|→∞, x∈Ω_0} |x|^{2/(p-1)} φ(x) > C when the exponents satisfy 2p/(p+1) ≤ q < p. Does that same blowup criterion remain valid throughout the larger range 1 ≤ q < 2p/(p+1)?
accepted.context_brief: Blowup-from-growth criterion below the scaling threshold

evidence.quote: Theorem 2.5 Assume that 2p/(p + 1) ≤ q < p and that Ω contains a cone Ω0. There exists a constant C = C(Ω0) > 0 such that if φ satisfies lim inf |x|→∞, x∈Ω0 |x|^{2/(p−1)}φ(x) > C, (2.1) then T∗ < ∞.
Open problem 2. Does the result of Theorem 2.5 remain valid when 1 ≤ q < 2p/(p + 1) ?

accepted.question_text: In the whole space R^N, consider the equation u_t - Δu = |u|^{p-1}u - b|∇u|^q in the scaling-invariant case q = 2p/(p+1). Theorem 2.8 constructs positive radial backward self-similar blowup solutions of the form u(t,x) = (T-t)^(-1/(p-1)) W(x/(T-t)^{1/2}) for 0 < b < 2 and for p in a non-explicit interval 1 < p < p_0(b,N). What are the actual admissible values of p for such self-similar blowup, can the existence result be extended to all p > 1 and all b > 0, is the self-similar solution unique for fixed parameters, and is the profile from Theorem 2.8 the universal blowup profile in the critical case q = 2p/(p+1), or can qualitatively different blowup profiles occur?
accepted.context_brief: Existence, uniqueness, and universality of critical self-similar blowup

evidence.quote: Theorem 2.8 Assume Ω = R^N, q = 2p/(p+1), and 0 < b < 2. There exists p0 = p0(b, n) > 1, such that for all p with 1 < p < p0, the equation (1.6) has a solution of the form (2.5) with m = 1/2, where W is positive, C^2, radially symmetric and radially decreasing in R^N.

Open problem 3. The value of p0 in Theorem 2.8 is not explicitly known (because the proof involves a limiting argument). Can one specify the allowable values of p, or even extend the result to all p > 1, and also to all b > 0? On the other hand, is the self-similar solution unique for each value of the parameters? Is the self-similar profile of Theorem 2.8 representative of all blowup behaviors when q = 2p/(p + 1), or do there exist different profiles?

accepted.question_text: For solutions of u_t - Δu = |u|^{p-1}u - b|∇u|^q with exponents in the range 2p/(p+1) < q < p, determine the true finite-time blowup rate as t approaches the blowup time T. In particular, is the correct order of growth ||u(t)||_∞ ≍ (T-t)^(-q/(2(p-q))) in this parameter range?
accepted.context_brief: Blowup rate above the scaling threshold but below q=p

evidence.quote: Open problem 4. What is the blowup rate when 2p/(p + 1) < q < p ? On the basis of the blowup profiles found in [12] in that range of parameters, and of the parabolicity of the problem, one could conjecture a rate of the order (T − t)^(−q/2(p−q)), but there no evidence that this guess is true.

accepted.question_text: For the semilinear parabolic problem u_t - Δu = |u|^{p-1}u - b|∇u|^q, what can be said about boundedness versus unboundedness of global-in-time solutions in the intermediate exponent regime 2p/(p+1) < q < p, excluding the already studied one-dimensional case q = 2? In particular, do all global solutions remain bounded, or can unbounded global solutions occur more generally in this range?
accepted.context_brief: Boundedness of global solutions in the intermediate q-range

evidence.quote: Theorem 2.11 Assume Ω = (0, L), 0 < L < ∞, p > q = 2. For some b = b0(L) > 0, there exist (infinitely many) φ such that ut ≥ 0, T∗ = ∞, and limt→∞ ku(t)k∞ = ∞.
Open problem 5. What can be said about boundedness of global solutions for 2p/(p + 1) < q < p, q 6= 2?

accepted.question_text: When q ≥ p, can the equation u_t - Δu = |u|^{p-1}u - b|∇u|^q on a domain Ω ⊂ R^N with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions admit finite-time blowup for some nonnegative initial data? This is known to be impossible in bounded domains, and Theorem 3.2 rules it out when the initial data are compactly supported even in unbounded domains, but the general case in unbounded domains remains unresolved. Does there exist any domain and any admissible initial datum for which finite-time blowup occurs when q ≥ p?
accepted.context_brief: Possibility of finite-time blowup in the regime q ≥ p

evidence.quote: Open problem 6. Can finite time blowup occur when q ≥ p ? This is unknown even for Ω = R^N (note that the existence of a blowing-up solution in some domain Ω would imply the same conclusion in R^N by comparison).
Theorem 3.2 Assume q ≥ p and Ω ⊂ R^N (bounded or unbounded). If φ is compactly supported in R^N, then T∗ = ∞.

accepted.question_text: Assume q ≥ p and let Ω be an unbounded domain whose inradius ρ(Ω) = sup_{x∈Ω} dist(x,∂Ω) is infinite. Theorem 3.1(ii) shows that some initial data then produce solutions that become unbounded, but this unboundedness may occur either in finite time or only as t → ∞. Theorem 3.5 gives genuine unbounded global solutions when Ω contains a cone. Does there exist an unbounded global solution for every domain with ρ(Ω)=∞ whenever q ≥ p?
accepted.context_brief: Existence of global grow-up for all infinite-inradius domains

evidence.quote: ρ(Ω) = sup{ r > 0; Ω contains a ball of radius r } = sup x∈Ω dist(x, ∂Ω).
Theorem 3.1 Assume q ≥ p. (ii) If ρ(Ω) = ∞, then there exists φ such that the solution u of (1.6) is unbounded (with either T∗ < ∞ and lim supt→T ∗ ku(t)k∞ = ∞, or T∗ = ∞ and limt→∞ ku(t)k∞ = ∞).
Open problem 7. Does there exist unbounded global solutions whenever ρ(Ω) = ∞ and q ≥ p ?

accepted.question_text: For unbounded global solutions of u_t - Δu = |u|^{p-1}u - b|∇u|^q, determine the precise asymptotic grow-up rate of ||u(t)||_∞ as t → ∞. In particular, for the solutions produced in the proof of Theorem 3.6, can the currently rough bounds C_1 t ≤ ||u(t)||_∞ ≤ C_2 e^{C_3 t} be sharpened to an exact asymptotic growth law?
accepted.context_brief: Precise grow-up rate for unbounded global solutions

evidence.quote: Open problem 8. What is the precise grow-up rate of ku(t)k∞ for unbounded global solutions of (1.6) ? For the solutions constructed in the proof of Theorem 3.6, we only have the rough estimate C1t ≤ ku(t)k∞ ≤ C2e^{C3t}, as t → ∞.

accepted.question_text: Let q ≥ p and Ω = R^N. For an unbounded solution, define the blowup set E = { x_0 ∈ R^N ∪ {∞} : there exist x_n → x_0 and t_n → T^* with u(t_n,x_n) → ∞ }. Theorem 3.7 states that in R^N either E = R^N ∪ {∞} or E = {∞}. Theorem 3.6 provides examples of the first alternative, where the solution diverges at every spatial point as t → ∞. Does there also exist initial data for which the second alternative occurs, namely E = {∞}, so that the solution becomes unbounded only by escaping to spatial infinity and not at any finite spatial point?
accepted.context_brief: Whether the blowup set can be only infinity in R^N

evidence.quote: Theorem 3.7 Assume q ≥ p and Ω ⊂ R^N (unbounded). Assume that φ is such that u is unbounded, with either T∗ < ∞ or T∗ = ∞. (ii) If Ω = R^N, then either E = R^N ∪ {∞} or E = {∞}.
Open problem 9. Does there exist φ such that E = {∞} when q ≥ p and Ω = R^N ? Theorem 3.6 provides some φ such that Ω = R^N and E = R^N ∪ {∞}.
